name: Data Collection
description: Learn about Data Collection and its applications in physics.

content.overview: So you've got your experiment set up—now comes the part where you actually gather your evidence. Data collection isn't just 'oh yeah, I measured something.' It's recording things properly, right in the moment, so future-you can actually use it. {{viz:diagram-01}}
content.explanation:
Think like a detective jotting down clues at a crime scene—sloppy notes mean a case you can never solve. Here's how to collect data like you mean it:

**1. Be careful and precise.** Use your tools the right way. Read measuring devices at eye level. Don't rush—rushing is where mistakes sneak in.

**2. Record immediately.** Write down measurements the second you get them. Don't trust your memory—it's worse than you think. Write the actual number, not 'about 5.' Write 5.2.

**3. Be consistent.** Measure the exact same way every single time. Always measure height from the same point. Always time things the same method.

**4. Record units. Always.** '5' alone means nothing. '5 meters' means something. Never leave the units off.

**5. Do multiple trials.** One measurement is just luck wearing a disguise. Three or more? Now that's actual data. {{viz:formula-01}}

**6. Watch for weird results.** If one measurement looks way off from the rest, flag it. Something probably went wrong—note it down instead of quietly ignoring it.

**Here's the difference in action—measuring a pendulum's period:**
- Wrong: 'Period is about 2 seconds'
- Right: Trial 1: 2.04 s, Trial 2: 2.06 s, Trial 3: 2.03 s

See the difference? One of those you can actually trust and build on later. {{viz:chart-01}}
keyPoints: Record numbers immediately—never rely on memory
Measure the exact same way every single time
Do multiple trials, not just one
Flag mistakes or unusual results instead of hiding them
Write clearly so someone else could actually read it
content.whyItMatters: Sloppy data collection can ruin an entire experiment—no amount of clever analysis fixes bad data. Careful collection upfront saves you time later and gives you results you can actually stand behind.
